title: Agent Skills vs 1 Big Prompt
description:
What are Agent Skills? Agent Skills explained in 60 seconds: a skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file, and your AI agent reads its full instructions only when a task needs them.
Agent Skills vs 1 big prompt: before, every rule you wrote loaded on every task; now each skill costs about 100 tokens until a task matches it.

Read the open standard and try it: https://agentskills.io/what-are-skills

Chapters
0:00 Why one big prompt fails
0:18 Agent Skills: a recipe box
0:28 How a skill loads
0:42 The how, and the lesson

The story: a cook who rereads every rule in one giant binder before frying one egg is your AI agent with one big prompt. A recipe box fixes it: every card has a tab (its name, and when to use it), the cook reads only the tabs and pulls the one card an order needs. Agent Skills work the same way. A skill is a folder with a SKILL.md file. At startup the agent loads only each skill's name and description (about 100 tokens each). When a task matches a description, it reads that skill's full SKILL.md. Extra files, such as references and scripts, load only if needed. So the agent keeps many skills on hand, and its context keeps room to work. Agent Skills is an open standard, started by Anthropic.

The takeaway: don't tell your agent everything. Tell it where to look.

Try it: make a folder with a SKILL.md whose frontmatter has a name and a description that says what the skill does and when to use it, then put the steps below it. Install skills only from sources you trust: a skill can tell an agent to run code.

Sources
Agent Skills specification (folder + SKILL.md, loading levels, ~100 tokens of metadata): https://agentskills.io/specification
What are skills (discovery, activation, execution; open standard): https://agentskills.io/what-are-skills
Claude docs, Agent Skills overview (loading levels and token costs; skills vs prompts; the pdf-processing example): https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/overview
Claude Code docs, skills (vs pasting the same instructions, vs CLAUDE.md): https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills
Anthropic engineering, "Equipping agents for the real world with Agent Skills" (2025-10-16): https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/equipping-agents-for-the-real-world-with-agent-skills

The binder, the egg, the soup and the rule names on screen are invented examples, not figures from a source. The "100 tokens" is the docs' "~100 tokens" per skill, rounded.
